subject: Question on hierarchical regression with autoregressive error

messages.author: 268807ff6f08a14c
messages.subject: Question on hierarchical regression with autoregressive error
parts:
Dear List,

first of all, let me wish you a Happy New Year!

I wonder if anyone could help me with a problem on a hierarchical linear regression with autoregressive terms.I am trying to analyse how much X different predictors (time series, dummy variables and their interactions)  contribute to an outcome y. As the time series I want to predict is not stationary and frequentist regression results in residuals with autocorrelation, my idea is to eventually code for an ARIMA(X) regression model, and, given that I have different subjects, a hiearchical model possibly even including a lag. I started building the model increasing the complexity (first just a linear model, then just an MA(1) term and now I also included the AR(1) term). The estimation is somehow slow but it did the job until now pretty accurately. With the inclusion of the AR(1) term, however, it estimates all parameters except the phi for the fictive 5 time series I simulated using the arima.sim routine. I have been trying to get my head around if there is anything wrong with the code but I cannot see anything. So my question would be if I am missing something obvious in model, i.e. is it right the way I am coding the ARMA term? Also, if there is anyone one who could come up with a way to optimise the code for a faster estimation I would be more than happy. Thanks in advance,

Best wishes

David
 

P.S.: Apologies, for posting this twice but my first (identical) post is deleted as it was without a category.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question on hierarchical regression with autoregressive error
parts:
Nothing jumps out at me here for either efficiency or
coding. But I'm not familiar with some of these parameterizations.

When you say it estimates all parameters other than phi, you
mean it recovers them in the appropriate posterior intervals over
simulated data? What happens to phi? This can sometimes happen
when the model's not identified, which will cause wide posterior
intervals on the non-identified parameter and slow sampling (even
if it's technically identified softly by a prior but not the likelihood).

This kind of thing is dangerous:

sigma_y = sigma_y_norm / sqrt(sigma_y_raw);

as you're building in a non-identifiability between sigma_y_norm
and sigma_y_raw (if they both go up, sigma_y stays the same).

And we don't recommend these hard constraints on parameters

real<lower=1, upper=80> nu_sigma_y;
...
nu_sigma_y ~ gamma(2, 0.1);

You can vectorize that final normal sample, but that's unlikely
to be the bottleneck. For even more efficiency, you could group
the data by s[t] so you could share scale parameters---but as I
said, I doubt the normal is the bottleneck here.

How are the n_eff for the correlation Cholesky factor?

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question on hierarchical regression with autoregressive error
parts:
Yes. No idea what's going on with phi then. Are you sure
you're not getting the right answer? That is, maybe the right
answer is very little time series effect based on previous value.

Isolating phi, you give it a prior

phi ~ normal(0,1);

and use it to generate epsilon[t] with a negative phi[s[t]] * y[t - 1]
term:

for (t in 2:T)
epsilon[t] = y[t] - (mu[s[t]] + y_temp[t] + phi[s[t]] * y[t-1]);

And then it shows up in the linear predictor as

for (t in 2:T)
y[t] ~ normal(mu[s[t]]
+ y_temp[t]
+ phi[s[t]] * y[t - 1]
+ theta[s[t]] * epsilon[t - 1],
sigma_y[s[t]]);

If you expand out epsilon[t-1], you get:

y[t] ~ normal(mu[s[t]]
+ t_temp[t]
+ phi[s[t]] * y[t - 1]
+ theta[s[t]] * (y[t - 1]
- mu[s[t - 1]]
- y_temp[t] +
- phi[s[t - 1]] * y[t-2])),
sigma_y[s[t]]);

where

y_temp = rows_dot_product(x, beta[s]);

So you get two terms in y[t - 1] and one in y[t - 2] that
may be close to canceling each other out:

phi[s[t]] * y[t - 1]

- theta[s[t]] * y[t - 1]

- theta[s[t]] * phi[s[t - 1]] * y[t - 2]

So the question is whether you're recovering the parameters from
simulated data within the posterior intervals. And if not, it may
be the identifiability issues raised from the above (phi[s[t]] and
theta[s[t]] are strongly anti-correlated and if y[t - 1] and y[t - 2]
are similar and s[t] and s[t - 1] are similar, it's going to cause
another kind of cancellation.

- Bob








P.S. Tabs in code are bad news, especially when mixed with spaces.

you were right, it was the right answer! I was just simulating the wrong thing. So I am simulating an ARMA error term, while I am trying to estimate an autoregressive term in the data. Cheers
David
